title: Nifty edges up to 25,299 for third straight gain as realty jumps; rupee slips to 94.03
dek: Foreign investors' buying in November is the strongest since September 2024, but auto and FMCG shares fell and the rupee weakened.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Indian shares ended a volatile session slightly higher on Thursday. The Nifty 50 rose 44.30 points, or 0.18%, to 25,299.35, its third straight gain, while the Sensex added 31.61 points, or 0.04%, to 81,911.01, according to market reports. Both indices are up about 10% so far in November, one report said.

Smaller companies did better: the Nifty Midcap 100 rose 0.85% and the Smallcap 100 1.12%. Realty was the strongest sector, up about 4% (reports differ between 3.7% and 4.5%), while auto and consumer goods fell about 1%. HDFC Life, Shriram Finance and Bajaj Finance led the Nifty's gainers; Hindustan Unilever and Mahindra & Mahindra were among the biggest losers.

Foreign portfolio investors bought Rs 12,563 crore of shares on Wednesday, and their net purchases in November have reached $6.43 billion, the most in a month since September 2024, one report said. The rupee fell 34 paise to 94.03 to the dollar, according to one report, and Brent crude traded near $92 a barrel.

Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments said flows and lower crude prices were the key supports, according to reports. Investors are also watching US bond yields, close to 5% on the 10-year Treasury, and Nvidia's results on 17 November after the resignation of its chief executive.
